assumptions.per_claim_limit_exemption_rationale: Diagnostic and dental categories have their own, larger sub_limit values (10,000 each) which already function as the practical per-visit ceiling; the flat 5,000 per_claim_limit is a consultation/pharmacy/vision/alt-medicine guardrail. Documented assumption, not stated explicitly in policy_terms.json.
assumptions.submission_date_assumption: ClaimSubmission.submission_date defaults to treatment_date when not supplied, since this exercise has no live submission timestamp. In production the API request time would be used instead, and the submission_deadline_days rule below would be meaningful for every claim rather than a no-op for the provided fixtures.
assumptions.ytd_claims_amount_assumption: annual_opd_limit and family_floater.combined_limit enforcement rely on ClaimSubmission.ytd_claims_amount (amount already paid out this policy year for that member/family). This is caller-supplied ground truth here because there is no persistent claims ledger in this exercise; it defaults to 0 (first claim of the year) when omitted. A production system would compute this from its own claim store instead of trusting the caller.
assumptions.pre_auth_validity_assumption: pre_authorization.validity_days (30) cannot be enforced without a pre-auth issuance timestamp, which is not part of any input in this exercise. Any pre_auth_id supplied is treated as currently valid. Documented limitation.
assumptions.pre_existing_condition_assumption: waiting_periods.pre_existing_conditions_days (365) is not enforced: distinguishing a genuinely pre-existing condition from a newly diagnosed one requires medical history beyond a single visit's diagnosis text, which this system does not have. Only the blanket initial_waiting_period_days and the named specific_conditions are enforced.
assumptions.branded_generic_drug_assumption: opd_categories.pharmacy.branded_drug_copay_percent and generic_mandatory cannot be applied per-line-item because extraction does not classify a medicine as branded vs. generic (that requires a drug database lookup, out of scope here). The flat pharmacy copay_percent (0%) is applied instead, and a WARN trace event flags this limitation for manual reviewer awareness on pharmacy claims.
